original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live PR overlap first, price both suppliers and distinguish a search best from an optimum. Report the word's packing cap from ceiling.ceiling() and the fraction of it realized; label packing gains as such.

first_step.inspect: Locate the selected packing source in the review and check live PRs for the same residual problem.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An actual paid-profile gain can improve the frontier up to the other supplier cap.
allowed_variations: One bounded residual packing instance or exact relaxation.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Rerunning an existing search with only a different seed as a separate mathematical contribution.

actual_scope: A chronology-aware packing bound for PR2571 and every nonnegative integer uniform initial shift of the unchanged PR2530 whole-helper inventory: a 102-group Hall cut, exact per-pattern cost dual, and strictly stronger ceiling than the window-free fractional pattern LP.
scope_change_reason: The selected-packing card is refined from the historical selected T16 packing to the live explicit owner-order residual in PR2571, following PR2530. The fetched PR2571 order is shifted by four; the bounded extension covers its entire nonnegative integer uniform-shift family.
bottleneck_link: A 114-bin width-eight shortage survives every uniform initial delay. Pricing it closes about 1e-7 of the primitive-endpoint relaxation gap and identifies nonuniform scheduling or a changed inventory as necessary to escape this cut.
stop_rule: Stop after an exact strengthened bound with source binding, positive primal control and rejecting controls, or hand off a precise failed implication. No new supplier or kappa claim.
evidence: README.md scoped proof; CERTIFICATE.json exact replay; INPUTS.json immutable predecessor pins; verify.py standard-library checker.

open_questions.question: Can a nonuniform stage shift escape the named 102-group cut while retaining a favorable complete bill?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every nonnegative uniform initial shift has at least 114 bins without a width-eight role.
open_questions.first_step: Give these groups at least 147 eligible calls, then recheck all other window and inventory cuts before physical realization.
open_questions.blocked_by: A changed order, literal whole-helper fill and complete native/global admission.

open_questions.question: Can coupled width-seven and width-eight cut constraints strengthen the bound?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A width-seven shortage alone admits zero-reduced-cost substitution by two width-eight roles.
open_questions.first_step: Combine that substitution with the rank-eight availability inequality in one rational dual.
open_questions.blocked_by: An exact feasible stronger dual; this package does not claim a packing optimum.
